title: Detect short-lived concurrency spikes and isolate traffic
author: Anika Rao
release_notes: Adds a short-lived concurrency spike detector plus an adaptive isolation rollout guard. The feature detects transient concurrency-driven tail-latency spikes, automatically isolates affected traffic slices, and runs targeted probe replays before resuming normal routing. Improves stability for bursty request patterns without manual intervention.
description:
Context and motivation: We've seen several incidents where short-lived concurrency spikes (bursts of lateral fan-out from edge services, client-side retries, or cold-request storms) produce transient tail latency spikes that our existing canary signals smooth out or miss because they average over longer windows. These spikes harm user-perceived latency and cause noisy alerts during rollouts. This PR introduces a detector designed to surface and act on short bursts that are causally correlated with concurrency changes and to isolate only the affected traffic slice until the spike subsides.

What this PR does (single summary): Implements a short-lived concurrency-spike detector that uses temporal de-blurring across percentile surfaces, a causal correlation heuristic between concurrency and p95/p99 deltas, and an adaptive isolation rollout guard to quarantine affected traffic slices and run targeted probe replays before resuming a rollout. The detector is lightweight, sampling-aware, and integrates with the existing perf-canary routing control plane.

Design notes and algorithm: The detector computes per-route percentile surfaces sampled at 1s resolution and performs a lightweight temporal deconvolution to separate fast spikes from slower drift. It then applies a causal score combining: (1) delta in concurrency (short window) normalized by expected concurrency distribution, (2) aligned p95/p99 spikes after a short propagation lag, and (3) sampling-weighted confidence. When the causal score crosses a high threshold, the rollout guard takes these steps: (a) mark a traffic slice as degraded, (b) shift that slice to a soft-isolated pool with reduced concurrency cap, (c) schedule probe replays that mirror the original requests at low rate, and (d) monitor probes for recovery for an adaptive hold period before unisolating.

Operational safeguards: - Sampling-aware scoring prevents noisy detection on low-volume routes. - A two-step action model (soft-isolation then probes) prevents full rollbacks for transients. - Configurable backoff and decay windows allow ops to tune sensitivity. - Integrated metrics are exposed to the console: spike_count, average_isolation_duration, probe_success_rate, causal_score_histogram.

Testing and validation: Unit tests across detection thresholds and sampling corners, synthetic load simulation harness (added to perf-canary/bench) to validate isolation behavior under controlled bursts, and a canary staging rollout in us-west-2 with 5% traffic to observe real traffic behavior. We ran multiple replay scenarios; probes correctly detected recovery in 97% of synthetic bursts.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag (off by default). 2) Enable for non-critical routes (canary tag) at 1% traffic for 48 hours. 3) Increase to 10% and monitor new console metrics and alerts for 72 hours. 4) Enable global by percentage and remove feature flag after 2 weeks if no regressions.

Related work: Builds on prior canary detectors (temporal-window detectors and ensemble evaluators) but focuses on sub-minute spike isolation instead of gradual drift. See ENG-1289 for signal spec and ENG-1302 for rollout guard contract.

Notes for reviewers: Main files to review are the detector implementation and the guard integration; other changes are tests and telemetry additions. The PR intentionally keeps default sensitivity conservative. Feedback requested on threshold defaults and metric names.
commits_summary: 5 commits: add spike detector core, add isolation guard plumbing, add probe replay scheduler, add unit tests + synthetic harness, update docs/console metrics.
review_comments: Marco Silva (reviewer): The deconvolution step looks compute-heavy for 1s resolution across many routes. Did you validate CPU overhead on the aggregator?

Author (Anika Rao): Yes — we implemented an efficient FFT-based streaming deconvolution with a capped window (max 60s) and fall back to EWMA when route QPS < 50. Measured +3% CPU on the aggregator under our staging load; added a feature toggle for the deconvolution module.

Priya Menon (reviewer): Suggest exposing the isolation-duration histogram to the alerts team so they can tune decay windows dynamically. Also would like a knob to limit concurrent isolated slices per route.
Author (Anika Rao): Added metric average_isolation_duration and a concurrency cap per-route config (defaults to 3). Updated docs and console dashboard to show these metrics.
Elijah Carter (reviewer): Integration tests flaked once due to scheduling in replay_scheduler — the sleep/polyfill caused timing races. Can we make replay scheduling deterministic in tests?
Author (Anika Rao): Rewrote the scheduler to accept a test clock injection; updated tests accordingly. CI rerun passed.
Marco Silva (approver): LGTM after addressing CPU and metrics feedback. Approved for merge with squash.
Release manager (comment): Please ensure feature flag is documented and ops notifies SRE on the 10% ramp.
checks: bench: pass (no regression >1% on p50/p95 in synthetic harness)
notes_for_ops: Feature behind feature flag perf.short_spike_isolation=false by default. Default sensitivity conservative; config at perf-canary/config/defaults.yaml. Notify SRE before ramping above 5%. Dashboard available at console -> Spike Isolation.
changelog_entry: Added short-lived concurrency spike detector and adaptive isolation rollout guard to perf-canary (feature-flagged).
risk_assessment: Low-medium: default conservative settings and multi-step isolation minimize blast radius. Potential CPU cost on aggregator under heavy route counts; we added toggle and EWMA fallback.
testing_notes: Synthetic harness scripts added. Tests include corner cases for low-sampling routes and concurrency cap enforcement. Staging rollout observed 97% probe recovery on synthetic bursts.
external_dependencies: None new; reuses existing telemetry and routing APIs.
